question: Should OpenClaw publish a supported OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and if so should it cover HTTP endpoints only, Gateway RPC schemas, or the public SDK path?
rationale: The implementation shape defines a public API, auth, versioning, and client-generation contract across stable Gateway surfaces, so automation should not choose it without maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Keep Open For API Direction
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported OpenAPI/schema scope and security/versioning contract before any generated artifact or runtime route is added.

options.title: Scope To A Generated Spec
options.body: Sponsor a narrow PR that generates a checked-in or served spec for selected Gateway HTTP endpoints with docs, auth warnings, and drift checks.

options.title: Fold Into SDK Track
options.body: Close or redirect only after maintainers decide that the public SDK/WebSocket client track is the sole supported custom-client path.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For API Direction
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported OpenAPI/schema scope and security/versioning contract before any generated artifact or runtime route is added.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the strongest recent history for the Gateway client/protocol package extraction and adjacent API-contract docs.
